newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S. Korea oil refining surplus seen for four years.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea oil refining surplus seen for four years.

text.p: South Korea's oil refining surplus is likely to be in place for a few more years and could force the sector to cut production rates, a senior official of the Korea Energy Economics Institute (KEEI) said on Tuesday.
Speaking at a fuels and lubricants conference in Singapore, Young-Seok Moon estimated the refining sector had a surplus capacity compared with domestic consumption of 229,000 barrels per day (bpd).
A copy of his presentation was made available to the press.
The South Korean refining sector has grown dramatically since 1964 when it had a capacity of just 35,000 bpd.
By the end of 1996, crude processing capacity had grown to 2.438 million bpd, with the addition in 1996 alone of 620,000 bpd.
Moon said the surplus would not clear until the growth in demand, which he forecast at an annual 4.6 percent, had overtaken capacity.
He forecast the refining sector would show a deficit in production of 8,000 bpd by 2000, increasing to 444,000 in 2006.
"The overall products balance and the threat of imports from outside the region lead us to conclude that refiners have to suffer from a drop in utilization rates," he said in the paper.

Moon, who is director of the petroleum policy division of KEEI, said fastest growth for product demand in South Korea was expected from gasoline consumption, although the government planned to hike transportation tax to curtail its consumption.
The affect of South Korea's expanded processing capacity has already been seen on the Singapore products market. In recent months South Korean refiners have been selling gas oil aggressively.
But the latest data indicates utilisation rates are high for now.
The Korea Petroleum Development Corp said earlier on Tuesday that the sector's operating rate was 99 percent. The data covered November, the latest period available.
The highest utilisation was at Ssangyong with 119.72 percent, and the lowest at Yukong Ltd with 85.34 percent.
